title: A Safehouse for the Extraction
premise: Coral Galloway, a crash investigator whose husband and daughter died in row twelve of Flight 419, lives off-grid in a network of safe houses protecting witnesses whose testimony powerful governments buried. When one safe house is listed for sale online — with photos revealing its hidden occupants and a coded ledger in the background — Coral realizes someone inside her network sold them out. Racing across three countries with the witnesses she swore to protect, she must deliver the ledger proving the crash was sabotage to an international tribunal while an assassin, hired by the same consortium that downed Flight 419, picks off her contacts one by one. In the end Coral trades herself for the witnesses' safe passage, testifies from a witness box instead of the shadows, and learns that belonging means standing in the light, even when it makes you a target.
about_author: Ivo Thornbury is a former aviation insurance adjuster turned novelist who spent a decade reading crash reports and the silences between them. He writes from a farmhouse in the Scottish Borders, where he keeps a wall of unsolved accident clippings he refuses to explain.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Opening on the anniversary of Flight 419, Coral works a cold crash file in her basement office, avoiding the memorial she never attends. A flashback to identifying her family's belongings establishes her grief and her obsessive precision. Emotional beat: grief hardened into method.

chapters.title: The Quiet List
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Her colleague Devi sends a link: a rural safe house — hers to manage — is listed for sale, with interior photos. One photo shows a child's drawing on the wall and the edge of a coded ledger. Coral's blood runs cold. Emotional beat: the vertigo of being seen.

chapters.title: Twelve Minutes to Clear
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, tense and procedural. She calls the protocol: burn papers, move the witnesses — a whistleblower chemist, Marek, and his teenage daughter Lena — within twelve minutes. The house is empty when a black SUV cruises past at dusk. Emotional beat: controlled panic.

chapters.title: The Man Who Buys Houses
chapters.summary: Assassin's POV (unnamed, called 'the Appraiser'). Cold, professional, he tours the listed property and reconstructs who lived there from scuff marks and a thermostat schedule. He reports to a voice called Vessel. Emotional beat: dread through competence.

chapters.title: Network of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She convenes the scattered network by burner phone: Ruthie the forger, Okafor the ex-diplomat, Devi. Someone inside had access to the listing photos. Trust fractures. Emotional beat: paranoia in a family built on secrecy.

chapters.title: What Marek Knows
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. In a motel outside Rotterdam, he finally tells Coral why he ran: the chemical signature in Flight 419's fuel was deliberate, and the ledger names the consortium — and three governments that licensed it. Coral realizes row twelve was not random. Emotional beat: grief weaponized.

chapters.title: The Listing Agent
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She traces the real estate listing to a shell brokerage and stakes out the office. The agent is a cutout — but her phone's last contact is a number Coral recognizes. It belongs to Ruthie. Emotional beat: betrayal's first sick lurch.

chapters.title: Confrontation in a Laundromat
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She corners Ruthie among spinning machines. Ruthie swears she was framed — her credentials were used, her flat tossed. A tail follows Coral out; she loses him in the tram tunnels. Emotional beat: trust extended on faith, not proof.

chapters.title: Vessel
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV. Vessel, a consortium fixer, briefs three government liaisons via encrypted call. The ledger must not reach the tribunal in The Hague. The Appraiser is authorized to 'liquidate the asset network.' Emotional beat: institutional evil, banal and vast.

chapters.title: The Chemist's Daughter
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Bored, scared, sharp-tongued, Lena hacks the motel's business center to check her mother's old social feeds — and pings a tracker. She hides the mistake, then confesses to Coral. Emotional beat: guilt, and the first real bond between them.

chapters.title: Border Crossing at 3 A.M.
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The team moves Marek and Lena across the Belgian border in a hearse Ruthie procured. A checkpoint almost breaks them; Coral talks her way through with a forged death-transport permit. Emotional beat: found family functioning under pressure.

chapters.title: Okafor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. He reveals the ledger is only half the proof; the other half sits in a diplomatic pouch he buried during his career, in a Geneva storage vault with a 72-hour access window. Emotional beat: an old man choosing to burn his last protection.

chapters.title: The Appraiser's Method
chapters.summary: Assassin's POV. The Appraiser interrogates the real estate agent, learns the network's next waypoint, and executes her cleanly. He keeps one of the listing photos — the child's drawing — for reasons he doesn't examine. Emotional beat: the first crack of humanity in a killer.

chapters.title: Geneva, Window Open
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The team splits: Coral and Okafor to the vault, Devi and Ruthie to shadow the tribunal clerk who can admit the evidence. Geneva is beautiful and full of watchers. Emotional beat: hope that feels like a trap.

chapters.title: Vault 44
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, high tension. Inside the storage facility, the Appraiser is already waiting — not to kill, but to offer Coral a trade: the pouch's contents for the witnesses' lives. She refuses; a firefight wrecks the vault corridor. They escape with the pouch, but Okafor is shot. Emotional beat: the cost of refusal.

chapters.title: Triage in a Chapel
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Hiding in a lakeside chapel, Lena — who shadowed her father's lab work — stabilizes Okafor while Coral rages at herself. Marek confesses he nearly took the Appraiser's deal years ago. Emotional beat: forgiveness as survival.

chapters.title: The Second Photo
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Studying the listing photos again, Coral notices a reflection: the photographer's silhouette wears a network-issue jacket. The mole photographed the house personally. She narrows it to Devi — or someone wearing Devi's kit. Emotional beat: suspicion turning inward.

chapters.title: Devi's Alibi
chapters.summary: Devi's POV. Devi proves her kit was stolen during the Rotterdam motel stay — meaning the mole was close enough to touch her things. The circle tightens to Ruthie, Okafor, or Coral herself. Emotional beat: a family interrogating itself.

chapters.title: Ruthie's Confession
chapters.summary: Ruthie's POV. Ruthie admits she sold access once — years ago, for her brother's medical debts — and has been paying for it since. The Appraiser blackmailed her into the listing. She gives Coral his dead-drop schedule. Emotional beat: shame transmuted into courage.

chapters.title: Dead Drop
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral runs the dead drop herself, feeding the Appraiser a false waypoint. But the drop's return signal contains a photo of Lena sleeping — taken hours ago, from close range. Emotional beat: terror in the shape of tenderness.

chapters.title: Inside the Circle
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, unraveling. The photo was taken with Coral's own camera, missing since the hearse crossing. The mole has been inside the vehicle, inside their trust. She says nothing — and starts watching everyone she loves. Emotional beat: loneliness at the center of the family.

chapters.title: The Tribunal Clerk
chapters.summary: Devi's POV. Devi and Ruthie meet the clerk, who reveals the tribunal can only accept evidence through a state sponsor — and all three implicated governments are blocking. The ledger needs a fourth door. Emotional beat: the law itself locked against them.

chapters.title: A Journalist Who Owes Okafor
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV, from his hospital bed in a safe flat. He directs them to Adaeze Nwosu, an investigative journalist he once protected, who can publish the ledger even if the tribunal stalls. Publication is the fallback — and a death sentence for its sources. Emotional beat: legacy and debt.

chapters.title: The Appraiser's Album
chapters.summary: Assassin's POV. The Appraiser reviews his own file on Coral and finds Vessel has appended a new order: after the witnesses, Coral herself — and a note that her family's crash file is flagged 'original authorship.' He begins to wonder who Vessel really serves. Emotional beat: a tool developing doubts.

chapters.title: Mole in the Hearse
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, the trap. Coral stages a fake itinerary known only to the whole team. The Appraiser hits the fake waypoint — meaning the mole acted, but under duress: the drop signal was Ruthie's blackmail code, triggered automatically. The real mole is someone with network root access. Emotional beat: relief that curdles.

chapters.title: Root Access
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, devastating clarity. Root access belonged to the network's founder — a man officially dead for six years: Elias Wren, who built the safe houses, and who Coral once loved. He isn't dead. He sold the listing to flush the ledger into the open for his own buyers. Emotional beat: betrayal by the person who taught you to trust.

chapters.title: Elias
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, flashback interleaved with the present. Coral reconstructs Elias's fall: his daughter died on a different flight, in a different cover-up, and he decided no tribunal could ever be trusted — only leverage. He wants the ledger to auction, not to publish. Emotional beat: grief as a rival religion.

chapters.title: The Auction
chapters.summary: Vessel's POV. Vessel meets Elias to bid for the ledger on the consortium's behalf. Elias strings him along, planning to sell to the highest of the three governments. Vessel, reading him, quietly authorizes the Appraiser to erase both Elias and the ledger. Emotional beat: predators circling each other.

chapters.title: Lena's Bargain
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena contacts Elias directly — she found his back channel — and offers to deliver the ledger if he spares Marek. Elias agrees, moved despite himself by a girl who reminds him of his daughter. Emotional beat: a child out-negotiating the monsters.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Room
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral plays her own hand: she leaks to all three governments simultaneously that the ledger will be published at dawn unless each grants one witness asylum. Now every government must protect the evidence to control it. Emotional beat: turning the machinery of power against itself.

chapters.title: The Handover at the Docks
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, set-piece. The exchange with Elias happens at Rotterdam docks at night. The Appraiser arrives to kill everyone. In the chaos, Elias takes a bullet meant for Coral — his last act ambiguous: sacrifice or theft. Coral grabs the ledger and runs. Emotional beat: love and betrayal in the same wound.

chapters.title: What the Appraiser Saw
chapters.summary: Assassin's POV. Wounded, the Appraiser reviews Vessel's orders and finds his own name on the post-operation cleanup list. He makes an uncharacteristic choice: he sends Coral Vessel's location and the cleanup schedule, then disappears. Emotional beat: a killer buying back his soul with a tip.

chapters.title: Vessel's Last Meeting
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, infiltration. Using the Appraiser's intel, Coral records Vessel meeting the government liaisons, capturing them ordering the Flight 419 cover-up in plain language. The recording plus the ledger is now undeniable. Emotional beat: the trap closing on the powerful.

chapters.title: Dawn Publication
chapters.summary: Adaeze's POV. At dawn, Adaeze publishes everything: ledger, recording, the row-twelve sabotage. Governments scramble to condemn their own liaisons. The tribunal clerk calls Devi: the evidence is admitted. Emotional beat: truth as a detonation.

chapters.title: The Price List
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Retaliation begins: safe houses burn, contacts vanish, Marek is taken. Coral realizes publication without protection was half a victory. The only currency left is herself. Emotional beat: the bill arriving.

chapters.title: The Trade
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, climax. Coral offers Vessel the one thing he needs — her public recantation and silence — in exchange for Marek, Lena, and the network's survivors. The exchange happens in a border hangar. She walks into custody with the truth already loose in the world. Emotional beat: sacrifice as the final act of belonging.

chapters.title: The Witness Box
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Months later, at the tribunal, Coral testifies publicly — no safe house, no alias — naming names while the world watches. Vessel's consortium fractures as allies defect to save themselves. Emotional beat: grief finally given a courtroom.

chapters.title: Verdict
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs, brief. Verdicts land; two governments fall, one limps on. Lena starts university under her real name. Ruthie forges nothing but paintings. The Appraiser is spotted once, unremarkable, alive, free. Emotional beat: imperfect justice, real enough.

chapters.title: A House With Windows
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, coda. Coral buys a small house — listed openly, photos and all — with curtains she never closes. Devi, Ruthie, and Lena come for Sunday dinner. On the wall hangs a child's drawing recovered from the first safe house. She leaves the porch light on. Emotional beat: belonging chosen in the light.

chapters.title: Row Twelve, Revisited
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, final chapter. On the next anniversary, Coral finally attends the memorial. She reads the victims' names aloud, including her family's, and adds a line to the crash file she keeps: 'Cause established. Accountable.' Then she closes the file — not the case, the file — and walks home in daylight. Emotional beat: grief integrated, story complete.
